question: Why a loaded game's second sort holds back more divisions than its first.

addresses.name: CAIUnit::SetPlanStance
addresses.comment: **Slot 77.** 0x4C36F0 to the `ret 4` at 0x4C38BD. Sets `this->+0x80` (stance_set) = 1 first; then, only if the agent has a unit: posts `CSetPlanAttributesCommand(unit, stance, 3, 3, -1000, -1000)` (ground stance only; 3 and the negatives are the command's leave-alone sentinels), **calls slot 77 with the same stance on every child agent** (CAIAgent +0x44 list, depth first, so the commands queue parent first), then CAIUnit::UpdatePlanAxis (0x4C3330); when the stance is 0, CAIUnit::RebuildOpsAreaProvinceRecords(this, &this->+0x90) (0x4BCD60); then CAIUnit::ScoreOpsAreaProvinces (0x4BD270); then every division on the held-back vector +0x15C has its `+0x2C8` (held-back) byte cleared, `this->+0x86` (replan_subordinates) is set for each, and the vector is emptied. So a change of stance releases the agent's reserve and asks for a slot-78 pass. Callers: CEU3AI::UpdateUnitStances at 0x491B92 (only when the value changes) and the interface. **Confirmed live 2026-11-11** (FINDINGS-liveread.md, section 45): Japan's Zhengzhou HQ on entering August 1938 sorts at stance 3 as bound, is posted stance 2, and its reserve - cleared here (0x4C386A) - is decided again by the next sort, seven held where five were.
addresses.evidence: Held-back marks logged at 0x4B298B and 0x4B3243, slot 69 and the recall watched, and the image scanned for writes to +0x2C8, on the running game entering Ireland1938_08_03_14, 2026-11-11.
